st.headline: Toyota and Honda may get stuck with the bill for Trump’s Canada tariffs
st.teaser: The United States remains Toyota and Honda’s biggest market.
fullText: TOKYO – US President Donald Trump is targeting Ottawa with a proposed 50 per cent tariff on Canadian car imports – but Japan’s Toyota and Honda may end up footing the bill.
The two Japanese automakers account for more than three-quarters of all cars made in Canada.
They could be forced to shutter some production lines if the tariffs go into effect on Jan 1, 2027, as proposed, analysts said.

While a deal could still be reached, the timing of the US tariffs could not be worse, as Japanese automakers are being stung by competition from low-cost Chinese electric vehicles in markets such as South-east Asia, Europe and Latin America.
The United States remains Toyota and Honda’s biggest market and, crucially, one where Chinese rivals like BYD are not allowed in.
Canadian-built cars accounted for almost a quarter of Honda’s US sales and 17 per cent of Toyota’s in 2025 , the most among major automakers, according to Barclays analysts.
As a result, the two face the biggest potential hit from Trump’s plan to double the levies from the current 25 per cent.
“If you really wanted to destroy the Canadian auto industry, you could with these tariffs,” said Julie Boote, autos analyst at Pelham Smithers Associates in London.
Both companies would likely have to close some of their Canadian assembly lines, she said.
Canada’s auto industry produces around 1.2 million cars a year and indirectly supports some 427,000 jobs.
Toyota’s exports from Canada to the US include the RAV4, while Honda exports the CR-V.
Both cars are among the best-selling sport utility vehicles in the US.
The proposed tariffs are the latest example of Trump trade policies that have left the global auto industry scrambling to adapt.

For years, US, European, Japanese and South Korean car companies and their suppliers built production chains across North America, taking advantage of cross-border trade deals and, especially in Mexico, lower labour costs.
But cost dynamics have now changed drastically.
US tariffs cost Toyota about 1.4 trillion yen (S$11.2 billion) in the 2025 financial year.
Toyota is now doubling down on US production.
The world’s largest automaker in 2025 said it aims to invest up to US$10 billion over five years to expand its US operations.
That will include a new $3.6 billion auto plant in Texas, where it intends to move production of the Tacoma pick-up truck from its Baja California plant in Mexico.
For Honda, which is struggling to turn around its money-losing car business, tariffs have only added to the strain.

A senior executive recently told reporters that it might not build an eighth assembly plant in North America unless the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) free trade talks among the US, Canada and Mexico are extended.
USMCA is the revised version of the 1994 North American Free Trade Agreement trade pact and has been in place for six years.
Trump opted on July 1 not to renew it, subjecting it to annual reviews, although talks have continued.
in 2025 , South Korea’s Hyundai said uncertainty about USMCA was delaying its investment decisions.

If the tariffs take effect, Toyota and Honda would likely try to redirect Canadian-built vehicles to other markets and then try to find ways to make up supply for the all-important US market – hardly an easy task, analysts said.
US-bound vehicles are often tailored to the market’s needs and regulations, while factories elsewhere may already be operating near capacity.
“It would represent a major shift from the past,” said Seiji Sugiura, a senior analyst at Tokai Tokyo Intelligence Laboratory.
Two Japanese suppliers said they were unsure what would happen next and it remained, at least for now, impossible to plan, given that it was still uncertain whether the tariffs would go into effect.
“We’re trying not to overreact,” one of the supplier executives said. REUTERS

cna.headline: Pokemon World Championships coming to Singapore in August 2027
cna.teaser: The Pokemon World Championships will be held at Singapore Expo from Aug 13 to 15, 2027, with Championship Sunday taking place at the Singapore Indoor Stadium.
fullText: Pokemon fans, it's time to catch 'em all: The Pokemon World Championships is coming to Singapore in 2027.
The event will be held from Aug 13 to 15, 2027, at Singapore Expo, while the tournament's Championship Sunday is set to take place at the Singapore Indoor Stadium.

The announcement was made during the closing ceremony of the 2026 Pokemon World Championships in San Francisco on Sunday (Aug 30), local time. Singapore will host the annual tournament for the first time in 2027.

The Pokemon World Championships is the pinnacle of competitive Pokemon play, bringing together top players from around the world to compete for the title of World Champion, as well as prizes and other rewards. Competitions include the Pokemon Trading Card Game, Pokemon Video Game Championships (VGC) and Pokemon Go.
Further details on the 2027 championships will be announced at a later time.

listening.title: Singapore's Hawker Culture Gets Digital Boost
listening.transcript: As traditional hawkers in Singapore face rising operational costs, a new government-backed initiative aims to digitize their daily operations. By implementing e-payment terminals and online delivery platforms, older stallholders are finding it easier to reach younger, tech-savvy customers. However, some elderly vendors still struggle with the transition, highlighting the persistent digital divide in our silver generation.

economistArticle.title: The Price of Closed Borders: The Economic Impact of Aggressive Immigration Curbs
paras: Politicians often campaign on promises that sound reassuringly simple at the ballot box but prove excruciatingly complex in practice. Chief among these is the promise of a sweeping deportation campaign and tighter borders. While a hardline stance on borders may satisfy the anxieties of a domestic electorate, it ignores the structural dependence of modern economies on imported labor.

In sectors such as agriculture, hospitality, and residential construction, foreign-born workers represent the backbone of daily operations. A sudden shortfall in this workforce does not instantly inspire local citizens to fill the vacant slots; instead, it leaves crops to rot in fields and construction projects indefinitely stalled.

The immediate consequence of such a labor shock is the emergence of severe operational bottlenecks. As businesses compete fiercely for a dwindling pool of available staff, wage pressures inevitably surge. Far from being a win for domestic workers, these rapid wage increases are quickly offset by the rising costs of goods and services, which can exacerbate existing financial pressures and risk rekindling inflation.

Moreover, the macroeconomic impact extends beyond temporary supply chain snarls to constrain long-term growth. With domestic demographics skewed toward an aging population, immigration has long served as a vital demographic engine. Without a steady influx of working-age individuals, the potential growth rate of the economy faces permanent downscaling.

Ultimately, pursuing isolationist labor policies is an expensive endeavor. Governments must eventually reconcile national sovereignty with the unyielding realities of economic globalization. Restricting the flow of human capital may satisfy political rhetoric, but the inevitable price is a smaller workforce and slower growth.
economistArticle.cn: 政治家们在竞选时做出的承诺在选票箱前听起来往往简单得令人安心，但在实际操作中却证明是极其复杂的。其中最核心的承诺就是彻底的驱逐出境运动和更严厉的边界管制。虽然对边界采取强硬立场可能会缓解国内选民的焦虑，但它忽略了现代经济对进口劳动力的结构性依赖。在农业、服务业和住宅建设等行业，外籍工人是日常运营的支柱。这一劳动力的突然短缺并不会立即激发本地公民去填补空缺；相反，它会导致农作物在田里烂掉，建筑项目无限期停滞。这种劳动力冲击的直接后果是严重运营瓶颈的出现。随着企业为争夺不断减少的可用员工而展开激烈竞争，工资压力不可避免地飙升。这远非本地工人的胜利，因为这些迅速上涨的工资很快就会被商品和服务成本的上升所抵消，这可能会加剧现有的财务压力并有重新燃起通货膨胀的风险。此外，宏观经济影响超出了暂时的供应链混乱，进而限制了长期增长。由于国内人口结构向老龄化倾斜，移民长期以来一直是至关重要的人口引擎。如果没有稳定的劳动年龄人口流入，经济的潜在增长率将面临永久性的下调。最终，追求孤立主义的劳动力政策是一项昂贵的尝试。政府最终必须在国家主权与不可动摇的经济全球化现实之间做出妥协。限制人力资本的流动可能会满足政治辞令，但不可避免的代价是更小的劳动力规模和更缓慢的增长。

gems.s: While a hardline stance on borders may satisfy the anxieties of a domestic electorate, it ignores the structural dependence of modern economies on imported labor.
gems.why: This sentence uses a 'While...' contrastive clause to masterfully balance two opposing forces: the political desire of local voters versus the cold reality of economic structures. 句子利用“While”引导的让步状语从句，完美平衡了“政治选民焦虑”与“经济结构现实”这两股相互对立的力量，展现了极高的辩证思维与句式深度。
